newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Juppe popularity down again, poll shows.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Juppe popularity down again, poll shows.

text.p: The popularity of both French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe has slipped further, according to an opinion poll carried out shortly before Chirac called a snap parliamentary election.

The IFOP poll for the magazine L'Express released on Wednesday showed 64 percent of those asked had no confidence in Juppe, against 59 percent in February, while 34 percent did have confidence in him against 40 percent previously.
Fifty-seven percent were dissatisfied with Chirac, up from 51 percent, and 42 percent supported him, down from 47 percent.
The popularity of opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin was down two points, with 50 percent satisfied with him, while 48 percent expressed no confidence in him, up from 46 percent.
The survey sampled 947 people and was carried out on April 17 and 18.
